title: AA Batteries 8-pack

drivers.name: Price increase (5.5%)
drivers.evidence: Two recent high-price weeks (2026-09-28, 2026-10-05) saw sales 49 and 31 vs baseline 34.7; average x0.89. Price spike likely reduces demand. Noise-adjusted effect from 10 promotions shows price sensitivity.

adjustment.analysis: Baseline median is 34.7. No events or promotions in target week. Price increased 5.5% to $10.81, above regular $10.25. Historical data shows price spikes (e.g., 2026-09-28, 2026-10-05) caused sales drops to 49 and 31, respectively, vs baseline 34.7 — implying price sensitivity. Heatwave forecast (38°C) may boost demand for cooling-related batteries, but no past evidence links heat to sales. Past promotions show median uplift 1.31, but noise-adjusted 1.17; post-promo dip 0.94 (noise-adjusted 1.0). No promotion here. Price increase likely suppresses demand. Use noise-adjusted price effect from recent high-price weeks: median 31/34.7 = x0.89. Heatwave effect uncertain; no evidence. Apply x0.89 for price, no heatwave effect. Final multiplier shrunk toward 1.0 due to thin evidence.

brief:
PRODUCT: AA Batteries 8-pack | category Household | Store #12 (Austin, TX)
TARGET WEEK: 2026-11-30 to 2026-12-06 (8 weeks after the last week with sales data)

KNOWN PLAN FOR THE TARGET WEEK:
  events: none
  shelf price: 10.81 (+5.5% vs regular price 10.25)
  planner notes: Heatwave forecast: 38°C all week

STATISTICAL BASELINE (exponential smoothing of recent sales; it ignores events, promotions and prices):
  median 34.7 | 5%-95%: 17.5 - 59.2 | 10%-90%: 20.0 - 56.0

In the evidence below, 'vs baseline' = actual units / what this same baseline predicted for that week.
It is the multiplier that would have been right, so it maps directly onto median_multiplier.
This product's ordinary weeks already swing about +/-44% around the baseline, so a past effect smaller than that, seen only a few times, is mostly noise. The
'noise-adjusted estimate' is the effect shrunk toward x1.0 for that noise and the number of sightings.
